title: VPC Defense Stack: Terraform assembly for security groups, NACLs, private DNS and egress policy
creator: Ava Patel
description: Goal: deliver a single, composable Terraform assembly ("VPC Defense Stack") that codifies Redwoods' recommended security posture for Private/VPC deployments. This includes: (1) a set of canonical security group patterns (app-tier, control-plane, mgmt-bastionless), (2) NACL templates for subnet-level deny/allow baselines, (3) an optional private DNS forwarding/resolver configuration (private hosted zones + conditional forwarding to resolver endpoints), and (4) deterministic egress policies and auditable egress proxies/origination rules.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes clear variables for environment, prefix, allowed egress CIDRs, and logging config
Module supports both apply-time and runtime toggles for private DNS resolver vs cloud-managed resolver
NACL and SG changes are predictable: a safe default deny posture with explicit allow lists; plan shows no destructive changes for default upgrades
Automated healthchecks deployed alongside infra: egress probe Lambda + DNS resolution probe with metrics exported to Datadog/Prometheus
Integration tests (terratest) pass in staging AWS account and PRs include non-destructive plan outputs
Migration path documented for existing customers using older security modules (state-import steps and state move snippets)
design_decisions: Single composite assembly (root module) that delegates to smaller submodules: sg-core, nacl-baseline, dns-forwarder, egress-orchestrator. This balances discoverability with reuse.
Default to least-privilege (deny-all NACL + minimal SG ingress). Provide opt-in variables for allowed flows and ephemeral exceptions.
Healthchecks are implemented as a pair of small Lambda functions (egress-probe, dns-probe) published via module using source archive. Metrics emitted as statsd/OTel for easy ingestion.
State management: keep resources in same Terraform workspace/state as customer's VPC. Provide helper scripts for import+state mv for customers migrating from legacy modules.

Upgrade strategy uses explicit schema_version variable and bump-checks in CI. We avoid in-place renames of resources; when renames required, provide migration helpers and a documented two-step rollout.
Avoid opinionated runtime network proxies; instead expose hooks for customers to attach Redwood egress gateway or third-party proxy via outputs and well-documented inputs.
implementation_notes: Module inputs: environment, name_prefix, allowed_egress_cidrs (list), allowed_ingress_ports (map by role), enable_private_dns (bool-string), dns_forwarders (list), nacl_whitelist (list), enable_healthchecks (bool-string), monitoring_namespace
Module outputs: sg_ids, nacl_ids, private_zone_id, resolver_endpoint, egress_policy_id, healthcheck_endpoints
Resource naming: follow 64-char limit; include environment+prefix+resource-type. Document collisions and recommended truncation strategy.
Provider constraints: require Terraform >= 1.5 and AWS provider >= 5.0 (strings for module file). Use strict provider aliasing for multi-account scenarios.
Testing: terratest suites to validate common topologies (single AZ public+private, multi-AZ private-only). CI to run plan checks and run critical terratest flows on PR merge to staging.
Security review: secrets pulled from customer KMS; module never writes sensitive values to logs. IAM least-privilege policies documented in README.
Observability: default export to Datadog metric name redwood.vpc.security.egress_probe.{env} and DNS probe metric redwood.vpc.security.dns_probe.{env}.
Backward compatibility: include a compatibility flag legacy_name_prefix to maintain resource names for older customers when enabled.
Documentation: Confluence design doc (link below), example usage in private-deployments repo, and migration playbook with step-by-step CLI snippets.

migration_plan_summary: For existing customers using older security modules: (1) run terraform state list against old module to enumerate resources, (2) use terraform import for DNS resolver + healthcheck resources where necessary, (3) run terraform state mv for resource name changes using provided scripts, (4) apply in a maintenance window. Detailed scripts and examples are in the migration-playbook.md in the module repo.
qa_steps: Create a staging VPC using example/template and apply module with enable_healthchecks=true
Verify SG and NACL rules match expected defaults and that egress is blocked except allowed CIDRs
Validate private DNS forwarding by resolving a private host and checking resolver metrics
Trigger egress-probe to an allowed external IP and verify metric ingested
Run terratest suite and confirm zero destructive changes on upgrade
